issues.failure_explanation: For the Gaussian (squared exponential) kernel $\kappa(x,y) = \exp(-\|x-y\|^2/(2\sigma^2))$, Assumption 2.1 is satisfied with $\bar{\kappa}(x,y) = \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\kappa(x,y)$, meaning that $\bar{\bm{K}}(Y) = \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\bm{K}(Y)$. The general formula in Theorem 3.3 establishes that $\nabla F_M(Y) = \bm{W}(Y)\bar{\bm{K}}(Y)\bm{W}(Y)(Y - \bm{\Psi}_{\mathrm{MSIP}}(Y))$. In the specialization to the Gaussian kernel, $\bar{\bm{K}}(Y)$ is replaced directly with $\bm{K}(Y)$, omitting the factor $1/\sigma^2$ (or $\lambda$). Thus, the stated simplification is false whenever $\sigma \neq 1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the right-hand side of the unnumbered display by $\frac{1}{\sigma^2}$ (or $\lambda$ where $\bar{\kappa} = \lambda \kappa$), yielding $\nabla F_M(Y) = \frac{1}{\sigma^2} \bm{W}(Y) \bm{K}(Y) \bm{W}(Y) (Y - \bm{\Psi}_{\mathrm{MSIP}}(Y))$.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified gradient formula for the Gaussian kernel in Theorem 3.3 is incorrect by a factor of $\sigma^{-2}$, giving an incorrectly scaled gradient when applied with bandwidth $\sigma \neq 1$.
issues.title: Missing bandwidth scaling factor in Gaussian kernel gradient formula
issues.why_classification: Inserting the missing scalar factor $1/\sigma^2$ is a routine local correction that completely restores the result without modifying any proof architecture or weakening any substantive guarantee.
